title: Start Plus Rate
idea: A linear model is a starting value plus a constant rate, so the intercept and the gradient each mean something in context.
misconceptions: Interprets the gradient as a total amount rather than an amount per unit
Swaps the roles of the fixed charge and the rate
Uses the model far outside its sensible domain, e.g. negative time

estimate.basis: 150 spoken words a minute, plus each pause, 0.8 s for each cue and 2 s for each tap question with its longer feedback line. The two figures are the two recall versions. Player turns are player-paced and not counted.

notes: Builds on ex.functions.line-equation, Rook's own, so the recall uses his own.watched, own.not-watched, short-version and after lines.

No second-method section: the map lists no methods. All three of the skill's methods appear: constant differences in a table is the big idea, rate and start from the words is examples 1 and 2, and two data points is example 3.

AI-SL2.5.linear-model also covers piecewise linear models. Those are ex.functions.piecewise-model (AI HL), which builds on this one, so this script teaches the single straight-line part of the skill and leaves the piecewise misconceptions to that script.
The money in the stories is scrap, the game's currency (SPEC.md).
The turns use fn-ext-line-model (situation line-model). Its fallbacks are fixed and worked below.

Format 2 (FAL-1043): moved from approved back to draft until it passes the format 2 checks (#188, #190, #191). `node tools/explainer-scripts.mjs --todo` lists what is left: turn lines with numbers or story words, not-yet lines to key to misconceptions, repeated frames and jokes, and the figure.

problem.setup: The tower's generator holds 40 litres of fuel and burns 2.5 litres an hour. Find when the fuel runs out.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Now one that goes down. The generator holds forty litres of fuel, and it burns two point five litres an hour.
beats.caption: Now one that goes down. The generator holds 40 litres of fuel, and it burns 2.5 litres an hour.

board.write: Generator: 40 L of fuel, burns 2.5 L per hour. When does it run out?

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: You build the model. I'll keep the channel open.

ask.prompt: Which model gives the fuel F litres after h hours?

right.speaker: rook-dead-air
right.say: Forty at the start, two point five less every hour. Lekker.
right.caption: Forty at the start, 2.5 less every hour. Lekker.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: The start is forty litres. Each hour takes two point five away, so the rate is minus two point five. F equals forty minus two point five h.
not_yet.caption: The start is 40 litres. Each hour takes 2.5 away, so the rate is −2.5. F = 40 − 2.5h.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: The gradient is minus two point five. Litres per hour, going down.
beats.caption: The gradient is −2.5. Litres per hour, going down.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Runs out means F is zero. Add two point five h to both sides, then divide. h is sixteen. Sixteen hours.
beats.caption: Runs out means F = 0. Add 2.5h to both sides, then divide. h = 16. Sixteen hours.

board.write: The fuel runs out after 16 hours.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: So the model only holds from zero to sixteen hours. Past sixteen there's no fuel to burn.

problem.setup: A water truck is being filled from the tower's well. After 4 minutes it holds 380 litres. After 10 minutes it holds 770 litres. The volume, V litres, after t minutes is modelled by V = mt + c.

parts.text: Find the value of m and the value of c.
Interpret, in context, the value of m and the value of c.
The truck is full when it holds 2000 litres. Find the time it takes to fill.
